target_customer: Software engineers and engineering teams that use AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex
problem: Running several coding agents at once on one codebase causes conflicts and makes review hard; developers need isolated workspaces and one place to review and merge agent work.
business_model: Freemium developer tool for Mac, with Pro subscription and a team cloud product

founders.name: Charlie Holtz
previous_startups: Melty (open source AI code editor, the YC S24 product that preceded Conductor)

founders.name: Jackson de Campos
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no background; a secondary profile says Netflix ML infrastructure and Brown, not opened.

exit.reason: Announced by CEO Charlie Holtz; deal terms undisclosed. Cloud shuts down Nov 20 2026 and local app support ends early 2027.

technical_complexity.rationale: Orchestrating agents in git worktrees with a native Mac UI, diff review and merge flow is solid product engineering; the underlying agents were built by others.

defensibility.rationale: Thin layer over agent CLIs and git worktrees; many open source clones and the model labs shipped similar apps (OpenAI Codex app, per a dev.to post).

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Labs and IDE vendors built parallel agent features; Meta acquired Conductor on 2026-11-04.

market_need_then: Developers began running multiple Claude Code sessions in mid 2025; the Conductor Show HN in July 2025 reached 228 points per a search summary. The company later cited 10x user growth since January 2026 and listed large tech company users, both self reported.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain founder voice with film references in blog posts

branding.brand_signature: Run a team of coding agents on your Mac
branding.community_and_virality: Show HN in July 2025 with 228 points, a Product Hunt launch, and podcast appearances such as Mastra.

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative single word name tied to orchestration, strong launch attention in the developer community and a Meta acquisition; name collides with other products called Conductor (for example Netflix's open source workflow engine).

pivots.from: Melty, an open source AI code editor
pivots.to: Conductor, a Mac app for running parallel Claude Code agents
pivots.why: Not stated by sources; the same workflow problem of juggling agents and verifying changes led to the new product.

outcome_analysis: Conductor started as the YC S24 company Melty, pivoted in 2025 into a parallel coding agent Mac app that spread quickly among developers, raised a 22M Series A in March 2026 and was acquired by Meta in November 2026. The exit came amid heavy platform risk, since model labs shipped similar apps, so it reads as a talent and product acquisition with undisclosed terms.
notes: Directory status says Active but sources dated 2026-11-04 report an acquisition by Meta, so exit is recorded as acquisition. The seed round was led by Matrix (per the Series A post) but amount and date are not stated; a Dealroom entry lists 125K USD from YC, unverified, so the seed round is recorded with amount and date as null, sourced to the Series A post (Ilya Sukhar at Matrix led it); the Dealroom 125K figure is not used. Total raised reported as about 24M USD. Aggregators date the Series A between March 30 and May 14 2026; the company's own post says March 30. Do not confuse with Conduct (London, 60M Series A). No dated competitor sources near the 2024 batch were found; list left empty. Search results mention a Melty Labs name; the company is formally Melty Inc.
